goal: Draft an onboarding checklist for a new data engineer

decisions.title: This agent needs 4 thing(s) from you before it is built

stages.name: understand
stages.label: Understand the request
stages.detail: What is asked, and what the build needs from you first.

layers.name: requirement_analysis
layers.label: Understand the request
layers.detail: Decides what you actually need, as a structured brief every later layer reads.
layers.summary: The verb 'draft' signals content generation from scratch rather than retrieval or analysis. While the output is a single artifact, it requires internal structure (timeline phases, categories, role-specific technical items) that must remain consistent, placing it at moderate complexity. No real-time data, uploaded documents, external systems, relationship graphs, or computation are implied by the request.

layers.name: agent_prerequisites
layers.label: Check what the build needs from you
layers.detail: Works out which credentials, service URLs and facts this needs, uses what the vault already holds, and asks you for the rest — before anything is built.

stages.name: equip
stages.label: Build missing tools
stages.detail: Writes and tests any tool the agent needs that does not exist yet.

layers.name: capability_gap
layers.label: Check for a missing capability
layers.detail: Decides whether the platform lacks a tool this request needs, and builds it.

stages.name: ground
stages.label: Gather what it can use
stages.detail: The tools, connectors and libraries available, the process knowledge and guidance in scope, and the kind of agent this is.

layers.name: agent_inventory
layers.label: Take inventory
layers.detail: Gathers the tools, integrations and documents this agent could be given.

layers.name: knowledge_context
layers.label: Knowledge context
layers.detail: Finds the business process this request belongs to and the build guidance in scope, and gives each later layer the part it needs.
layers.summary: Off — building without process knowledge. 7 guidance item(s) in scope (5 must/avoid).

layers.name: agent_archetype
layers.label: Choose agent types
layers.detail: Decides task, goal or conversational for each agent, the patterns it needs, and its oversight — from the process, the build guidance and the execution profile first.
layers.summary: The requested agent: conversational + tool_using_react, reflective. Decided 1 by llm. The work involves dialogue-driven customization (guidance:40) rather than open-ended goal pursuit (guidance:42), and layers tool-using ReAct with reflective checks because the output feeds concrete provisioning and staffing decisions.

stages.name: design
stages.label: Design the agent
stages.detail: Five independent decisions made at once, then checked against each other.

layers.name: agent_facets
layers.label: Decide tools, connectors, libraries, model and identity
layers.detail: Five independent decisions, made at the same time.

layers.name: tool_selection
layers.label: Choose tools
layers.detail: Decides which platform capabilities this agent needs.
layers.summary: The requirement is a pure text-generation task (all needs_* flags are false) asking for a generic, time-phased data engineering onboarding checklist. The agent can produce the entire deliverable from its own knowledge of data engineering practices without retrieving real-time data, querying documents, accessing external systems, or performing computations.

layers.name: connector_selection
layers.label: Choose integrations
layers.detail: Decides which external services this agent must reach.
layers.summary: The requirement is to generate a text-based onboarding checklist for a data engineer, which is a pure content generation task with needs_external_system explicitly set to false. No specific third-party product is named in the request, and the workspace has no registered connectors available to attach.

layers.name: library_selection
layers.label: Choose knowledge
layers.detail: Decides what documents this agent reads, and whether it reasons over the graph.
layers.summary: The requirement explicitly sets needs_documents to false and requests a general data engineering onboarding checklist that can be generated from standard industry practices (pipelines, warehouses, orchestration). No user-specific documents exist or are needed, so no library should be attached or created.

layers.name: model_selection
layers.label: Choose a model
layers.detail: Decides the model and how deterministic its answers should be.
layers.summary: This requires structured generation of a multi-dimensional checklist (time phases × categories) with data-engineering domain specificity, demanding the organizational and reasoning capabilities of mistral-large-latest. Temperature 0.2 ensures consistent, well-structured output at the low end of the structured generation range (0.2–0.4), minimizing hallucination of specific tool names that would require customization per the stated risk factors.

layers.name: identity
layers.label: Define the agent
layers.detail: Decides the tier, and therefore the name and remit.
layers.summary: The capability is specific to a single product type (data engineering onboarding) with unique deliverables (pipelines, warehouses, orchestration) that cannot be generalized to other domains or roles without fundamentally changing the agent's behavior. This aligns with Tier 3 (use-case) criteria.

layers.name: facet_consistency
layers.label: Check the decisions fit together
layers.detail: The model supports the tools and connectors chosen, is current, and document needs have a library.

stages.name: govern
stages.label: Provision and govern
stages.detail: Creates the library it was designed around, then its guardrails and rules.

layers.name: library_provisioning
layers.label: Provision documents
layers.detail: Creates the document library this agent needs, if it does not exist yet.

layers.name: guardrail_config
layers.label: Configure guardrails
layers.detail: Decides the moderation categories and thresholds Mistral enforces on this agent.
layers.summary: Agent holds no tools, integrations, or documents, and its subject (data engineering onboarding) is not a moderation topic category. Disabling moderation avoids unnecessary latency and false positives.

layers.name: rule_selection
layers.label: Choose rules
layers.detail: Decides which of your optional agent rules this agent must follow.
layers.summary: The agent generates structured onboarding checklists for data engineering roles and does not handle personal data, external systems, or real-time data. No optional rules are necessary to mitigate risks for this use case.

stages.name: author
stages.label: Write and create
stages.detail: Instructions that express every decision, then the agent on Mistral.

layers.name: instruction_authoring
layers.label: Write the instructions
layers.detail: Decides how this agent thinks, expressing every prior decision to the model.
layers.summary: Applied conversational patterns (guidance:41, 40, 50) to ensure the agent clarifies inputs before generating the structured checklist, with explicit defaults for unknowns to always produce an actionable, domain-specific draft.

layers.name: agent_assembly
layers.label: Assemble the agent
layers.detail: Validates the decisions together and creates the agent.

stages.name: verify
stages.label: Test the agent
stages.detail: Runs it on designed prompts and repairs its tools and instructions if it falls short.

layers.name: agent_evaluation
layers.label: Test the agent
layers.detail: Designs test prompts, runs the new agent on them, judges the answers, and rebuilds failing tools and revises the instructions when needed.

layers.name: execution
layers.label: Run the agent
layers.detail: Holds the conversation and executes any tools the agent calls.

requirements.intent: Create a structured, actionable onboarding plan to systematically integrate new data engineering hires into the team, covering technical setup, access provisioning, domain knowledge transfer, and early deliverables.
requirements.deliverable: A time-phased onboarding checklist (e.g., pre-start, day 1, week 1, first month) organized by category—access & security, tooling & environment setup, documentation & architecture review, team introductions, and initial hands-on tasks—specific to data engineering workflows (pipelines, warehouses, orchestration).
success_criteria: Organized by clear timeline phases (e.g., before day 1, day 1, week 1, month 1)
Includes data-engineering-specific items such as warehouse access, pipeline documentation, orchestration tools, and data modeling standards
Balances technical provisioning with team integration and business/domain context
Each item is actionable and assignable (owner + task, not vague aspirations)
risk_factors: Without organization-specific details, the checklist may reference tools or access patterns that do not match the actual tech stack, requiring customization before use
requirements.reasoning: The verb 'draft' signals content generation from scratch rather than retrieval or analysis. While the output is a single artifact, it requires internal structure (timeline phases, categories, role-specific technical items) that must remain consistent, placing it at moderate complexity. No real-time data, uploaded documents, external systems, relationship graphs, or computation are implied by the request.

decisions.name: The requested agent
decisions.rationale: Tailoring an onboarding plan requires dialogue to gather specific context about the new hire and team, tool use to access HR/access/documentation systems, and reflective validation since the plan drives access provisioning and resource decisions.

agent_config.description: Generates a structured, time-phased onboarding checklist tailored to data engineering roles, covering technical setup, access provisioning, domain knowledge transfer, and early deliverables.

outcomes.name: Prompt-injection screen
outcomes.message: In force — checked on every user message, on every answer.

outcomes.name: Read-only database
outcomes.message: In force — checked before every tool call.
